A.explanation: Gives $5.6 \text{ m}$, which is only two oscillations at $4A$ per oscillation. It undercounts the number of cycles in $20 \text{ s}$.

B.explanation: Gives $9.6 \text{ m}$, which is $4 \times 2.4 \text{ m}$. It wrongly uses the horizontal trough-to-peak distance instead of the vertical motion of the ball.

C.explanation: Gives $11.2 \text{ m}$, which is 4 oscillations each travelling $4 \times 0.70 \text{ m}$ vertically.

D.explanation: Gives $19.2 \text{ m}$, which uses the full wavelength $4.8 \text{ m}$ per oscillation. The ball does not travel horizontally with the wave.

hints: Notice the ball only moves vertically, so the $2.4 \text{ m}$ trough-to-peak horizontal distance does not set how far the ball moves.
The ball oscillates up and down with the wave frequency $0.20 \text{ Hz}$, so find the period $T = 1/f$ and how many oscillations fit in $20 \text{ s}$.
One full vertical oscillation is peak to trough to peak, a total path of $4$ amplitudes, so multiply $4 \times 0.70 \text{ m}$ by the number of oscillations.
walkthrough: The ball floats and moves only vertically, so it performs simple oscillation at the wave frequency $f = 0.20 \text{ Hz}$ with amplitude $A = 0.70 \text{ m}$.
Period of one vertical oscillation is $T = 1/f = 1/0.20 = 5.0 \text{ s}$.
Number of oscillations in $20 \text{ s}$ is $N = 20/5.0 = 4$.
In one oscillation the path is $A$ down to equilibrium, $A$ to trough, $A$ back to equilibrium, $A$ to peak, so distance per cycle $= 4A = 4 \times 0.70 \text{ m} = 2.8 \text{ m}$.
Total distance travelled by ball $= N \times 4A = 4 \times 2.8 \text{ m} = 11.2 \text{ m}$. This is option C.
